Ghana Medical Trust Fund explores partnership to expand access to diagnostic services
items.description: The Ghana Medical Trust Fund (GMTF) is exploring partnerships with leading diagnostic service providers to expand access to quality healthcare services for beneficiaries under its Patient Support Programme. The Administrator of the Trust Fund, Adjoa Obuobia Darko-Opoku, led a delegation on a working visit to MDS-Lancet Laboratories and Quest Medical Imaging to discuss possible areas of collaboration aimed at improving access to timely and specialised diagnostic services for patients. During engagements with the management of MDS-Lancet, led by its Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director, Dr Paul Sekyere-Nyantakyi, discussions focused on leveraging the laboratory’s nationwide network to provide reliable diagnostic services to GMTF beneficiaries. The parties also considered aligning services with the Trust Fund’s approved tariffs to promote efficient, transparent and sustainable healthcare delivery. The delegation toured MDS-Lancet’s laboratory facilities, including its phlebotomy and sample collection centre, microbiology, biochemistry, haematology and pathology units, as well as procurement, biomedical engineering, information technology, finance and logistics departments. The visit also included Quest Medical Imaging, where the team inspected facilities offering MRI, CT Scan, mammography, fluoroscopy, ultrasound and digital X-ray services. The Trust Fund said such partnerships will strengthen access to specialised diagnostics and help bring life-saving healthcare closer to more patients across Ghana.

items.title: Anass Salah-Eddine repousse l'option Olympiakos et prend son temps
items.description: L'avenir d'Anass Salah-Eddine reste incertain. Le latéral gauche international marocain aurait décidé de ne pas donner suite, pour le moment, à l'intérêt de l'Olympiakos, malgré des discussions avancées entre le club grec et l'AS Rome. Selon plusieurs médias néerlandais, les dirigeants de l'Olympiakos et de la Roma négocient actuellement un éventuel transfert du joueur de 24 ans et seraient proches d'un accord sur les modalités de l'opération. Toutefois, une source proche du joueur, citée par Hesport, affirme que Salah-Eddine ne souhaite pas, à ce stade, rejoindre le championnat grec. Le défenseur marocain préférerait patienter et attendre d'autres opportunités avant de prendre une décision concernant son avenir. Toujours selon cette source, l'Olympiakos pourrait revenir à la charge avant la fermeture du mercato estival. Néanmoins, la position du joueur n'aurait pas évolué. L'ancien pensionnaire du PSV Eindhoven souhaiterait étudier des propositions qu'il juge plus adaptées à ses ambitions sportives. Auteur d'une saison remarquée sous les couleurs du PSV Eindhoven, où il évoluait en prêt, Salah-Eddine a disputé 25 rencontres et délivré une passe décisive. Il a également participé à la Coupe du monde 2026 avec les Lions de l'Atlas, prenant part à quatre matchs durant le tournoi. À l'issue de son prêt, le défenseur est revenu à l'AS Rome avec l'ambition de convaincre le staff technique de lui accorder une place dans l'effectif. Son avenir demeure toutefois incertain, plusieurs clubs européens suivant de près sa situation. L'hypothèse d'un retour au PSV Eindhoven semble en revanche s'éloigner. Le directeur sportif du club néerlandais, Ernest Stewart, a récemment laissé entendre que cette piste n'était plus d'actualité, rappelant que le joueur avait choisi de retourner à Rome plutôt que de poursuivre son aventure aux Pays-Bas. À quelques semaines de la clôture du mercato, Anass Salah-Eddine continue donc d'évaluer ses options. Son choix devrait dépendre des offres qui se présenteront au cours des derniers jours du marché des transferts. The post Anass Salah-Eddine repousse l'option Olympiakos et prend son temps appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Les menaces réelles à la stabilité tunisienne
items.description: La dernière sortie du président algérien Abdelmadjid Tebboune sur la Tunisie **, que de nombreux Tunisiens trouvent déplacée voire insultante, repose la question des accords sécuritaires et de défense conclus le 7 octobre 2025 entre Tunis et Alger et surtout leur définition de la menace terroriste et leurs modalités opératoires, dont on sait très peu de choses. (Photo : Elyes Kasri * L’absence de communication à ce sujet de la part des autorités tunisiennes suscite de sérieuses appréhensions surtout au vu des nombreuses suspicions et même des confidences attribuées à d’anciens responsables sécuritaires algériens sur des liens troubles entre les services spéciaux du pays voisin et certains groupes terroristes et même, semble-t-il, certaines actions terroristes commises en Tunisie notamment au cours des années 2012-2013. La relation trouble du régime algérien avec le terrorisme et la quête démocratique nécessite une clarification des accords et des engagements sécuritaires et de défense bilatéraux afin d’éviter que la crainte de l’inconnu et des précédents attribués au régime algérien ne fassent passer la crise de confiance entre les deux peuples à un sentiment plus profond et plus durable de nature à creuser un fossé entre les deux voisins condamnés par l’histoire et la géographie à coexister pacifiquement et en bonne entente. Les Tunisiens qui brandissent l’épouvantail d’Israël et du sionisme international et ne prêtent pas attention à ceux qui vouent une haine tenace à la Tunisie et nourrissent des desseins maléfiques à son égard, gagneraient à regarder de plus près la véritable et actuelle menace à leur pays en se posant de simples questions : – qui occupe des territoires tunisiens riches en hydrocarbures et en ressources hydrauliques ? – qui assèche les cours d’eau qui ont depuis l’aube des temps irrigué la Tunisie ? – qui a enraciné la contrebande en Tunisie ? – qui a organisé des attaques et des actions terroristes contre la Tunisie comme à Gafsa en 1980 ? – quelles sont la nationalité et l’origine des dirigeants les plus sanguinaires des groupements islamistes qui ont sévi en Tunisie ? – qui inonde la Tunisie avec des migrants illégaux subsahariens qui la mettent dans une situation inextricable d’être considérée comme une menace à la citadelle Europe, pourtant notre principal partenaire économique, ou envisager un rapatriement dépassant les moyens logistiques disponibles ou contribuer au dessein déstabilisateur d’une guerre civile au risque d’un remplacement démographique ? – qui cherche à isoler la Tunisie sur la scène internationale en utilisant le chantage énergétique et terroriste ? – qui exprime par ses actions et ses propos le plus de mépris pour la Tunisie ? – qui cherche à gommer l’indépendance et la souveraineté de la Tunisie en la traitant ou même en la décrivant comme une province ? Un pays qui n’arrive pas à définir la menace réelle à sa stabilité et à sa souveraineté est une proie facile et à moitié conquise. * Ancien ambassadeur. ** S’exprimant devant la presse, le 27 juillet 2026, le président algérien a menacé, sans les nommer, ceux qui veulent «déstabiliser» la Tunisie. Il a employé une expression populaire algérienne virulente («nous détruirons la tente de ses parents») par allusion aux entités qui chercheraient à déstabiliser la Tunisie. Selon lui, la Tunisie est visée uniquement en raison de sa proximité avec l’Algérie. Traduire : certains acteurs chercheraient à fragiliser le voisin tunisien pour mieux isoler et affaiblir l’Algérie. items.description: Los trabajos nocturnos en el incendio de Fermoselle (Zamora) han permitido reducir “sustancialmente su peligrosidad” con la estabilización de los dos frentes que más preocupaban, el norte y el este, si bien se mantienen cuatro sectores activos con “numerosos puntos calientes y zonas muy complicadas”. Durante la noche se han evacuado dos nuevas poblaciones, Villar del Buey y Pasariegos. En total, 14 localidades han sido desalojadas por este fuego y están confinadas Fermoselle y Fariza. El operativo de extinción teme especialmente el viento que está previsto que se avive durante la tarde de este jueves y las altas temperaturas. items.title: Revue de presse de ce jeudi 30 juillet 2026
items.description: Voici les principaux titres développés par la presse nationale de ce jeudi 30 juillet 2026 Al Massae • À l’occasion du 27ᵉ anniversaire de la Fête du Trône, la province de Taounate a inauguré 11 centres de santé de nouvelle génération et remis les clés de 20 bus de transport scolaire au profit de plusieurs communes rurales, pour un coût dépassant 7,82 millions de dirhams. Ces projets s’inscrivent dans les efforts visant à renforcer les secteurs de la santé et de l’éducation, ainsi qu’à lutter contre le décrochage scolaire, notamment parmi les jeunes filles en milieu rural. Bayane Al Yaoum • Dans un contexte marqué par l’évolution rapide des rapports de force, l’émergence de nouveaux pôles économiques et la multiplication des défis sécuritaires et climatiques, le Maroc a su préserver l’indépendance de sa décision stratégique et conforter l’image d’un État qui définit ses positions en fonction de ses intérêts nationaux, tout en maintenant une ouverture et des relations équilibrées avec ses différents partenaires. Al Ahdat Al Maghribia • Vingt-sept ans après l’accession du Roi Mohammed VI au Trône, le bilan historique témoigne de réalisations majeures ayant concerné la modernisation des infrastructures, l’essor industriel, le développement des provinces du Sud, la promotion des énergies renouvelables, ainsi que le repositionnement stratégique du Royaume en Afrique et le lancement de l’ambition atlantique, jusqu’aux préparatifs engagés pour l’organisation de la Coupe du monde 2030. Ces acquis traduisent une vision royale marquée par sa cohérence et sa continuité depuis 1999, une constance dont la portée apparaît d’autant plus importante dans un contexte international profondément bouleversé par des mutations majeures et des crises successives au cours du premier quart du XXIᵉ siècle. • Le Royaume du Maroc se prépare activement à entrer dans l'ère de la quatrième révolution industrielle, où l'intelligence artificielle s'impose désormais comme un levier essentiel de développement de l'économie nationale et de consolidation de la souveraineté numérique. La transformation numérique n'est plus perçue comme un choix ou un luxe, mais comme une nécessité stratégique pour renforcer la compétitivité du pays aux niveaux régional et international. Assahra almaghribia • Le Roi Mohammed VI a adressé, mercredi soir, un Discours à la Nation à l’occasion du 27e anniversaire de l’accession du Souverain au Trône. Dans ce message, le Souverain a affirmé : « Aujourd’hui, la stabilité est la variable-clé dans l’équation du développement au Maroc. Elle est aussi le capital stratégique qui fait la fierté du pays ». • Le peuple marocain célèbre ce jeudi 30 juillet le 27ᵉ anniversaire de l’accession du Roi Mohammed VI au Trône. C'est une occasion nationale renouvelée pour se remémorer les grands chantiers de réformes et les réalisations qualitatives accomplis par le Royaume, lesquels ont permis au Maroc de renforcer sa capacité à relever les défis et d'affirmer sa présence sur les scènes régionale et internationale. Tout au long de ces vingt-sept années, le Royaume a consolidé, sous la conduite éclairée du Roi, une dynamique de développement fondée sur des réformes progressives, le renforcement de l'État des institutions, la modernisation des infrastructures et le lancement de projets stratégiques majeurs, tout en érigeant la diplomatie marocaine en acteur influent sur les questions régionales et internationales. • Le Président de la Chambre des Représentants, Rachid Talbi El Alami, a représenté le Roi Mohammed VI, mardi à Lima, à la cérémonie d’investiture de la nouvelle Présidente de la République du Pérou, Keiko Fujimori. Lors de cette cérémonie, qui s’est déroulée au siège du Congrès péruvien, en présence de Chefs d’État et de délégations étrangères, de représentants d’organisations internationales, de membres du corps diplomatique accrédité à Lima, ainsi que de plusieurs autres personnalités, Mme Fujimori a prêté serment en tant que Présidente de la République du Pérou. items.title: 2027: Quit if you can’t campaign for us, APC tells Tinubu’s ‘technocrats’
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, has warned political appointees serving in the government of President Bola Tinubu that they cannot hold political positions while claiming to be technocrats detached from partisan responsibilities, insisting that such appointees must be ready to mobilise support for the party or vacate their offices. APC national chairman, Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, gave the warning on Wednesday in Abuja when he received members of the Progressive Local Government Chairmen’s Forum, led by the Chairman of Chanchaga Local Government in Niger State, Dr Mustafa Jibrin, who briefed him on the group’s grassroots mobilisation drive ahead of the 2027 general election. Yilwatda said the council chairmen, being closer to the people than officials in Abuja, were better positioned to identify appointees who were failing to deliver politically in their wards, regardless of how well they performed administratively in their offices. “It is you who will tell me that this commissioner is not working. Maybe he is working in the office, but politically he is zero in his ward. It is you who know whether this director general may be working in the office, but politically he is zero back home,” he said. Yilwatda said appointees could not distance themselves from politics simply because their titles carried technocratic descriptions, comparing such claims to someone denying their ethnic identity despite carrying its unmistakable markers. “We call them political appointees. There is a word ‘political’ there. They are not just technocrats. They are political appointees. You can’t be holding a political position and then say you are not a politician. I have been hearing some people saying that, ‘I am not a politician,’ but they are holding political appointments. It is like somebody who has Yoruba or Kanuri tribal marks telling you that he is not a Yoruba or Kanuri man. It cannot happen,” he said. According to him, appointees who wanted to avoid politics altogether should decline political appointments in the first instance, adding that the party’s mobilisation efforts depended on votes rather than office holders who saw themselves purely as administrators. “If you don’t want to be a politician, don’t take a political appointment. We work to mobilise votes. Without the votes, you can’t be in office. That is why we need you to work with these people. Tell them they are not doing well. Tell them where we need to work harder. Tell them where we have leakages so that we can win the election,” he said. Receiving the briefing from the local government chairmen, Yilwatda assured the group of the party’s full backing for their mobilisation activities, including plans to inaugurate the forum’s state coordinators and organise a mass endorsement rally for the president in Abuja. “We will support you. We will stand by you. We will ensure that we have a strong partnership that will give this party a strong victory in 2027,” he said. Yilwatda pledged that the party would personally join any mobilisation efforts organised by the forum without waiting for formal invitations, likening reluctance to participate in such efforts to someone who is hungry but insists on being invited before eating. Earlier, Jibrin had informed the national chairman that the Progressive Local Government Chairmen’s Forum now had the backing of over 685 local government chairmen and 31 state governors under the platform, and that the group was targeting at least 70 per cent of votes cast in the 2027 election for the APC. He said the forum enjoys the support of the Governor of Niger State, Mohammed Umar Bago, who nominated him to lead the group, and disclosed plans to mobilise all 685 council chairmen, alongside their councillors, for a formal endorsement of President Tinubu’s re-election bid on a date to be fixed by the national chairman. items.title: New Zealand FM in row with Beijing's envoy after telling Chinese-born lawmaker to 'go back to your own country'
items.description: New Zealand’s top diplomat Winston Peters drew the ire of Beijing’s ambassador in Wellington on Thursday after telling a lawmaker of Chinese descent to “go back to your own country”. During a debate about New Zealand’s response to the Covid pandemic on Wednesday, populist NZ First leader Peters was asked by China-born Green Party member Lawrence Xu-Nan: “Are you vaccinated?” In response, Peters said the lawmaker, who was born in the Chinese city of Tianjin but grew up in Auckland, had “come here five minutes ago”. “Go back to your own country. That’s where they lie like a flatfish, but they don’t lie like that here,” Peters said. “This is called a democracy, unlike what you’re used to. Go back to where you’ve come from, you loudmouth.” The comments sparked a rare intervention from Chinese ambassador to New Zealand Wang Xiaolong. Wang said on X on Thursday that while he preferred to stay out of domestic politics, “suffice it to say, sometimes, a statement says more about the person that makes it than anything or anybody else”. Peters fired back at Wang, saying his comments had “proven my point”. “We live in a democracy that includes free speech and rights — those two values that other certain countries not only limit, but do so with force,” Peters said on X. “If that offends the pearl clutchers and the communist shills labelling it as ‘dangerous’ – welcome to New Zealand”. It’s not the first time Peters and his party — seen as kingmakers in New Zealand’s fractured political system — have received criticism for racist comments. Earlier this year Peters’ deputy Shane Jones criticised New Zealand’s free trade deal with India as risking a “ butter chicken tsunami ”. Last year Peters and Jones were forced to back down after the deputy yelled “send the Mexicans home” at MP Francisco Hernandez during a debate. Peters had followed up that comment by telling Hernandez, who was actually born in the Philippines, and Xu-Nan to “show some gratitude” for being in New Zealand.

items.title: ‘Thunder’ Balogun’s legacy must not die – Son
items.description: BY JACOB AJOM It’s exactly 54 years today that one of Nigeria’s greatest footballers, Teslim ‘Thunder’ Balogun passed on in his sleep in Ibadan, western Nigeria (now Oyo state). His death, according to Kayode Balogun, one of the late footballer’s children remains a mystery. Notwithstanding, Kayode is calling on both the federal and Lagos state governments not to allow his father’s legacy to die with him. In a chat with this reporter, he recalled in graphic detail how his father died. “When he got back home from work, the evening before his demise,” Kayode started, “ he was in his usual self, ebullient and cheerful. After dinner, we all went to bed; no complaints. Early in the morning, we were woken up by a loud scream from dad’s bedroom. It was mommy. When we rushed to the bedroom to find out what happened, we saw mom just screaming and pointing at our daddy, lying still on the bed. A few neighbours came in after hearing mom’s scream. She called a doctor who came in moments later and confirmed that our father was dead. Later they took the body to the morgue. Till date we still don’t know what killed him.” He was 45. Teslim Balogun was married to Alhaja Mulikat Abike Balogun, a former table tennis player. They wedded in 1955 before joining him in London in 1956 while he played for Queens Park Rangers. Balogun was Nigeria’s foremost footballer whose exploits were legendary. Apart from playing the game, he was also a coach. As a striker, Teslim was famous for his fearsome, powerful shot that earned him the nickname ‘Thunder’. Balogun also played for the Nigerian national team for 12 years and a member of the famous UK Tourists. He won the Governor’s Challenge Cup a record five times out of seven finals; played for several Nigerian teams like Marine Athletics, Pan Bank, Jos X1 UAC and Railway, as well as English clubs Peterborough United and QPR.(Queens Park Rangers). Balogun became the first African to qualify as a professional football coach. Kayode recalled, “while in England, the former Premier of Western Nigeria Chief Obafemi Awolowo persuaded my father to return and help develop the game in the region. He heeded the call, came back and took Western Nigeria to their first Challenge Cup triumph.” He later led the national team at the 1968 Summer Olympics in Mexico, where after two losses to Japan and Spain, held Brazil to a 3-3 draw. As a coach, the late Balogun concentrated on discovering and developing talent. He discovered, groomed and persuaded the late Chief Adegboye Onigbinde, coach Jossy Lad among others into football coaching. Engineer Olamide Balogun, one of the family’s seven children remembers his father as a loving family man. “He was a man who loved his children and ensured he was close to them. He visited us at school and helped in whatever way he could to make us happy and comfortable.” Kayode told this reporter that the biggest honour done to his late father by the Lagos state government was naming the multi-purpose stadium in Surulere after him, but regretted that not much is happening at the arena now. “Government must not allow my father’s legacy to die. There should be sporting activities there to keep the place booming. The post ‘Thunder’ Balogun’s legacy must not die – Son appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Pakistan says 'doing utmost' to bring US, Iran back to Islamabad MoU
items.description: The Foreign Office (FO) said on Thursday that Pakistan was doing its “utmost” to bring the United States and Iran back to the negotiating table under the Islamabad memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed last month. Addressing a weekly press briefing, FO spokesperson Tahir Andrabi said Pakistan noted with concern that the security situation in the Middle East “remains precarious despite the relative calm of the past few days, which had rekindled hopes that this positive development, this calm, would consolidate into a durable and fully respected ceasefire and pave the way for dialogue”. Andrabi reiterated Pakistan’s support for dialogue and diplomacy, maintaining that it remained the “only viable path forward”. “We welcome all efforts aimed at sustaining cessation of hostilities and resumption of dialogue between Iran and the US,” he said, adding that Pakistan remained engaged and will continue to do so. “Let me add that the negotiations between parties are ongoing to normalise the situation, particularly the situation in the Strait of Hormuz, as well as to de-escalate,” he stated. He added that Pakistan was doing its “utmost” to bring the two parties back to the Islamabad MoU “so that all irritants can be removed in the light of the spirit of the agreement and the Pakistan-Qatar joint statement on June 22”. Andrabi urged both the US and Iran to exercise “maximum restraint and fully adhere to their commitment to resume technical-level talks” in line with the Islamabad MoU and the Pakistan-Qatar joint statement. The MoU between the US and Iran was signed on June 18 after weeks of intensive diplomacy. It was aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz and ending the Middle East conflict — which began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February — after a further 60 days of negotiations. However, renewed hostilities erupted on July 7, when Iran attacked commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, including a Qatari liquefied natural gas tanker, accusing the US of violating the understanding. The attack prompted multiple waves of US strikes on Iranian military targets. The conflict has intensified with the Houthi rebels in Yemen imposing a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia, extending the war to a second major shipping chokepoint. On Wednesday, the war spread across new fronts as explosions hit a natural gas loading port in Egypt and a US-owned floating storage tanker was reportedly struck by a drone, while the US and Saudi Arabia carried out joint strikes on Iran-backed paramilitary groups in Iraq in retaliation for attacks on US troops and Saudi oil targets. On Thursday, after nearly a week-long pause, the US again struck Iran in retaliation for Tehran targeting American bases in Jordan. Documentary aired by DW ‘nothing but speculative commentary’ The FO spokesperson also “rejected” a documentary about Pakistan’s nuclear programme uploaded by Germany-based Deutsche Welle ( DW ) recently on its YouTube channel, terming it “misleading”. Responding to a query, Andrabi said the documentary was “nothing but a regurgitation of hackneyed and speculative commentary and biased sourcing”. “The documentary reflects either a profound misunderstanding of, or a deliberate disregard of the history, evolution and rationale of Pakistan’s nuclear programme,” he said. The FO spokesperson also commented on DW ’s decision to air the documentary: “By lending a platform to such poorly-sourced and one-sided content, DW risks undermining its own credibility and reputation for professional fact-finding journalism. “Responsible journalism demands rigorous verification, balanced context, not amplification of recycled conjecture and unfounded insinuations.” Andrabi called on DW to “exercise greater editorial responsibility when reporting on issues with far-reaching implications for international peace and security”. “Pakistan has full confidence in the robustness of its command and control architecture as well as comprehensive, technical, legal and institutional mechanisms governing the nuclear safety and security and our wider nuclear programme,” the FO spokesperson affirmed. He asserted that “these arrangements meet the highest international standards and have been consistently acknowledged by independent international experts”. FO highlights ‘India’s deep intolerance for independent voices’ Asked for a comment on India’s move to ban the social media accounts of state-run Pakistan TV for its residents, Andrabi quipped, “Does it surprise you?” Since tensions between Islamabad and New Delhi intensified last April in the wake of the Pahalgam attack — which also resulted in a brief military escalation — India has blocked access to several Pakistani social media accounts and YouTube channels . Andrabi said the Indian government’s decision to block access to social media accounts of Pakistan TV and others was “entirely in keeping with its established pattern of suppressing information and peddling an officially sanctioned and carefully sanitised version of so-called reality through pliant media that it has in its own country”. “Factual reporting has no place in the captive ecosystem prevailing in India. The frequent lapse into escapism exposes India’s deep intolerance for independent voices and its increasing reliance on repressive and restrictive measures as instruments of state policy,” he said. The FO spokesperson went on to urge the international community to take “full cognisance of the Indian government’s curbs on the media and the shrinking space for free [speech] in India”.

items.title: Eddie Howe leaves Newcastle after five years
items.description: Eddie Howe is leaving his role as Newcastle manager after five years at St James’ Park, the BBC and Sky reported on Thursday. The 48-year-old replaced Steve Bruce in November 2021 and won the League Cup in March 2025 — the club’s first major trophy since 1969. The former Bournemouth boss also led Newcastle to Champions League qualification in 2023 and 2025. But he came under pressure last season as the Magpies finished 12th in the Premier League, with 17 defeats in their 38 games. The club have been depleted by the departures of Sandro Tonali to Tottenham and England forward Anthony Gordon to Barcelona in recent weeks. Speculation continues over the future of captain Bruno Guimaraes. Howe’s final match in charge was a 4-1 defeat to Championship side Bristol City in a pre-season friendly on Wednesday. items.title: Les États-Unis mènent une "vague intensive" de frappes contre l'Iran
items.description: Les forces américaines ont mené, dans la nuit de mercredi à jeudi, une « vague intensive » de frappes contre l'Iran, en réponse aux « tentatives d'attaques de missiles » perpétrées contre les troupes US dans la région. « Les forces du Commandement militaire américain pour le Moyen-Orient (Centcom) ont mené à bien une vague intensive de frappes contre l’Iran, en réponse aux tentatives d’attaques de missiles perpétrées (mardi) contre les forces américaines », a écrit le Centcom dans un communiqué publié sur le réseau X. « Les forces du Centcom ont frappé des dizaines de cibles du corps des gardiens de la révolution islamique en Iran, notamment des centres de commandement militaires, des installations de missiles et de drones, des sites de surveillance et de défense côtières, ainsi que des moyens maritimes », a ajouté la même source. Selon le commandement militaire américain, « ces frappes visaient à réduire davantage les menaces que font peser l’Iran et ses mandataires sur les forces américaines, le transport maritime commercial et les pays voisins du Golfe ». U.S. forces began launching strikes against Iran at 8 p.m. ET today. The strikes are a powerful response to yesterday's attempted Iranian attacks on U.S. forces based in the Middle East. — U.S. Central Command (@CENTCOM) July 30, 2026 Cette annonce intervient après les déclarations mercredi du président Donald Trump, qui avait promis une riposte musclée contre l’Iran au lendemain de l’interception par les forces américaines d’une attaque de missiles balistiques iraniens visant les troupes américaines stationnées dans la région. « On va leur mettre une sacrée raclée (…) On va les frapper fort. Ils vont en prendre plein la figure », a déclaré Trump à la chaîne américaine Fox News. Le locataire de la Maison Blanche a ajouté que les forces américaines n’avaient eu que quelques minutes pour réagir à cette attaque surprise et avaient abattu les missiles avant qu’ils n’atteignent leurs cibles. items.title: France : La Cour des comptes épingle les résultats décevants des partenariats recherche publique-entreprises
items.description: La juridiction financiere dresse un constat sans concession sur la politique de soutien a la recherche partenariale. Alors que la France peine a atteindre l'objectif de 3 % du PIB consacre a la R&D, les dispositifs publics peinent a produire les effets escomptes sur l'innovation et la competitivite. Des investissements massifs aux effets limites Entre 2014 et 2024, l'etat a mobilise pres de 19 milliards d'euros en faveur de la recherche partenariale, avec un pic a 3 milliards en 2024 sous l'impulsion de France 2030. Pourtant, seulement 15 % a 20 % des entreprises innovantes externalisent une partie de leur R&D vers le secteur public. « Les resultats de la politique de soutien a la recherche partenariale sont mitiges, sinon decevants au regard des moyens mobilises », souligne la Cour dans son rapport. 🔬 Recherche publique-entreprises : malgré 19 Md€ d’aides entre 2014 et 2024, les partenariats restent peu développés. La Cour appelle à mieux cibler les soutiens, simplifier les dispositifs et valoriser l’engagement des chercheurs. #Recherche 👉 https://t.co/nYUwPzIwwB pic.twitter.com/M3L4nC7tiH — Cour des comptes (@Courdescomptes) July 27, 2026 Cette faiblesse s'explique par de fortes disparites : 54 % des grandes entreprises collaborent avec la recherche publique, contre seulement 11 % des PME. Si une correlation positive apparaît localement avec les depenses de R&D et l'emploi dans certaines categories d'entreprises, l'effet-levier global sur la depense interieure de recherche et developpement (DIRDE) reste imperceptible. Une strategie a refonder La Cour critique un empilement de dispositifs : LabCom, Carnot, CIFRE, chaires industrielles, appels a projets, souvent mal articules et insuffisamment evalues. Elle recommande d'elaborer un plan national clair, centre sur un nombre limite de priorites strategiques, de privilegier les cofinancements prives et de mieux articuler aides nationales et europeennes. Les poles universitaires d'innovation (PUI), crees en 2024, doivent etre perennises et rationalises pour ameliorer le service rendu aux chercheurs et entreprises dans un contexte d'austerite pour le budget de l'Etat francais . Les delais de signature des contrats, qui varient de 3,5 a 9,5 mois selon les sites, illustrent les lourdeurs persistantes. Valoriser les chercheurs impliques Enfin, la Cour insiste sur l'adaptation des regles de carriere : les activites de valorisation, d'expertise et de conseil avec les entreprises doivent etre mieux reconnues dans les evaluations, sans remettre en cause la recherche fondamentale. Des mecanismes d'interessement et une simplification des prestations de conseil sont egalement preconises. Ce rapport relance le debat sur l'efficacite de l'ecosysteme francais de l'innovation face a la concurrence internationale alors que la Cour des comptes avait deja alerte sur le retard pris par la France dans la quantique .

items.title: ‘We’re committed to increasing finance for Africa’ — CAF urges review of FIFA proposal
items.description: The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has announced plans to review FIFA’s proposal to open the commercial operations of the FIFA World Cup and other major tournaments to private investment. In a statement issued on Wednesday, CAF said its president, Patrice Motsepe, will meet with the Confederation’s Executive Committee next week to examine the proposal and determine Africa’s position. The African football body said its member associations would also have the opportunity to participate in the consultation process in line with FIFA and CAF regulations. “CAF also encourages its Member Associations to examine the FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal and participate in the consultation process in accordance with CAF and FIFA’s regulations and established procedures,” the statement partly reads. “CAF is committed to continue consulting and working together with its Member Associations, FIFA, other Football Confederations and stakeholders in support of increasing financial and other resources for the development and growth of football in Africa and worldwide.” The development follows FIFA’s announcement earlier this week that it intends to establish the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a new commercial subsidiary that would oversee the business operations of its flagship competitions, including the FIFA World Cup. Under the proposal, FIFA would retain majority ownership of the company while seeking to raise about $4.2 billion later this year by selling minority, non-controlling stakes to carefully selected long-term investors. The proposal has generated widespread debate across the global football community. British newspaper The Times reported that FIFA President Gianni Infantino could become commissioner of the new commercial entity after the expiration of his current term in 2031. The report also named venture capitalist Joshua Kushner and an investment arm of JPMorgan Chase among potential investors. Several football governing bodies have criticised the proposal. UEFA described the FIFA World Cup as “not an asset to trade,” while European Union Sports Commissioner Glenn Micallef urged FIFA to keep “hands off our game.” Football confederations in Europe, South America, North America and Asia have also expressed concerns, saying they were not consulted before the proposal was unveiled. The post ‘We’re committed to increasing finance for Africa’ — CAF urges review of FIFA proposal appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Destructions et stockage de nitrate d'ammonium, les pratiques israéliennes au Sud-Liban
items.description: Plus d'un mois apres la signature de l'accord-cadre entre le Liban et Israel , les operations de destruction menees par l'armee israelienne dans le sud du Liban connaissent une nette intensification. Dans la nuit du 28 juillet, des dizaines d'habitations ont ete dynamitees entre Tallousse et Markaba, dans le caza de Marjeyoun, effacant entierement un quartier. Ces demolitions interviennent alors que des negociations doivent reprendre a Rome du 4 au 6 août sur la mise en œuvre de l'accord conclu entre Beyrouth et Tel Aviv. Parallelement, la Force interimaire des Nations unies au Liban (Finul) a annonce avoir decouvert, plus tot ce mois-ci, pres de quatre tonnes de nitrate d'ammonium a proximite du village occupe de Houla, a rapporte le media libanais L'Orient-Le Jour . Rendre inhabitable le Sud-Liban Cette annonce, faite quelques jours avant le sixieme anniversaire de l'explosion du port de Beyrouth, a suscite de nombreuses speculations. Certains medias ont evoque une possible appartenance du stock au Hezbollah. Cette hypothese est toutefois rejetee par le general libanais a la retraite Khalil Gemayel cite par L'Orient-Le Jour , qui affirme que ce materiel aurait ete utilise par l'armee israelienne pour faire exploser des tunnels. Selon une source citee par des medias libanais, les conteneurs portaient d'ailleurs des inscriptions en hebreu. Au-dela de cette decouverte, l'ampleur des destructions nourrit les interrogations sur les objectifs poursuivis par Israel. Pour plusieurs analystes, ces demolitions viseraient a rendre durablement inhabitables les villages de la bande frontaliere afin de retarder le retour de leurs habitants. Le media libanais estime que l'objectif est de detruire les infrastructures civiles, habitations, ecoles et hopitaux, qui permettraient une reprise rapide de la vie dans ces localites. Cette intensification intervient peu apres le lancement des premieres « zones pilotes », prevues par l'accord-cadre et destinees a accompagner le retrait israelien en echange d'un renforcement du controle de l'etat libanais et du desarmement du Hezbollah. Toutefois, plusieurs informations relayees par la presse israelienne indiquent qu'Israel reste reticent a evacuer les secteurs occupes et pourrait chercher a maintenir, voire a etendre, sa zone tampon. Selon le general Gemayel, les destructions repondraient egalement a un objectif militaire immediat : eliminer toute presence potentielle dans les tunnels ou les bâtiments encore debout, alors que l'armee israelienne semble se preparer a une presence prolongee dans certaines zones du Sud-Liban.

items.title: Living wage, 2027 elections: NLC rallies workers for tough battles ahead
items.description: • Says fight for better Nigeria must be unwavering By Victor Ahiuma-Young As Nigeria inches closer to another round of national minimum wage negotiations and the 2027 general elections, the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, is expanding its agenda beyond the familiar struggle for higher wages. It is positioning organised labour as a decisive political and social force capable of influencing not only workers’ welfare but also the direction of governance in Nigeria . At its 2026 Rain School in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, the Congress unveiled what amounted to a broad ideological roadmap for the labour movement, calling on workers to prepare simultaneously for battles over a living wage, stronger labour protections, democratic accountability and greater participation in shaping Nigeria’s political future. Addressing participants including union leaders and labour activists from across the country, NLC President, Joe Ajaero, declared that the era of workers serving merely as voting blocs or passive spectators in Nigeria’s democracy must come to an end. Instead, he urged organised labour to rediscover its collective strength and prepare to become what he described as the country’s “critical force for change.” “The theme of this year’s school: The Working Class and the Politics of 2027, is deliberately chosen and profoundly strategic,” Ajaero said. “It declares that we, the producers of the nation’s wealth, refuse to be passive observers in the political process. We are the engine of the economy, the hands that build this nation, and we will not be treated as mere objects of political manipulation.” Workers can shape 2027 For Ajaero, the political significance of Nigeria’s workforce extends far beyond election-day voting. He argued that workers possess enormous industrial and political influence but have failed to deploy it effectively over the years. According to him: “While many of us workers may feel overwhelmed by rising inflation, stagnant wages and worsening living conditions, we remain the country’s greatest organised force. “When you look at your payslip and see a pittance that cannot feed your family, when you see the cost of food, accommodation, transportation and healthcare spiralling out of control, it is easy to feel powerless. “But you are not insignificant. You are the lifeblood of this nation. You are the critical force that can force change.” The NLC President insisted that if workers remained united and organised, they could significantly influence the outcome of the 2027 general elections. “The industrial and political power of a nation does not reside in its treasury or in political party offices. It resides in the palms of your hands and in the collective strength of your solidarity. “If we make up our minds and act unitedly, we will be in a position to define outcomes in the 2027 general elections.” Living wage Although the current national minimum wage stands at N70,000, Ajaero dismissed it as inadequate in the face of soaring inflation and the rising cost of living. He said: “The battle for a living wage will soon begin in earnest. The paltry sum that currently passes for a wage can no longer be sustainable. It is a poverty wage.” Rather than approaching negotiations from a position of weakness, he urged labour leaders to negotiate from a position of strength. “We must not go to the negotiation table with a begging bowl. We must demand a wage that truly approximates a living wage—a wage that enables workers to feed, house, educate and care for their families with dignity,” Ajaero said. He called on all NLC affiliates and state councils to begin mobilising immediately for what he described as one of labour’s defining struggles in the coming months. Review of labour laws Beyond wages, the Congress accused the Federal Government of deliberately delaying long-awaited labour reforms. According to Ajaero, despite years of negotiations and consensus among government, employers and organised labour, the reviewed Labour Administration legislation has remained stalled for about six years without being transmitted to the National Assembly. Ajaero said “We have laboured, we have negotiated, and we have reached consensus. Why the delay? This six-year delay is a deliberate strategy to maintain the status quo of impunity and exploitation. “A modern labour administration law is not a luxury. It is a necessity for protecting Nigerian workers and aligning our labour system with international best practices.” He lamented that Nigeria remains among the countries where workers’ rights are routinely violated through restrictions on union activities, collective bargaining and industrial action. “They attack our right to organise, to bargain collectively and to strike. They criminalise our struggles and use the instruments of state power to suppress dissent.” Beyond elections Ajaero sounded a note of caution that labour’s mission extends beyond electoral contests. He argued that the Congress must become a movement for democratic renewal and social justice. “The struggle is bigger than elections. It is a struggle to preserve the soul of the nation. We must build a democratic, welfarist-inspired alternative that places the needs of the people above the profits of the few”, he insisted. The NLC President did not spare his criticism for corruption, which he described as the principal reason workers continue to suffer despite Nigeria’s enormous wealth. “No matter how much we earn as a nation, if illicit financial flows and kleptocrats continue feeding on our resources, workers will keep bleeding. Nigeria is not broke. The political class is saving the nation’s wealth in their private bank accounts”, he lamented. The NLC President reminded participants that the Rain School was never intended to be merely an academic exercise. Instead, he described it as a strategic mobilisation platform for the struggles ahead. “This Rain School should not be a seminar. It should be a launchpad. “Let the knowledge you gain here be your ammunition. Let the solidarity you build here be your shield. Let the action you take when you return be your sword. “The future must be fought for. The future is not given to us. We must fight for it.bAnd we will win. “A people united can never be defeated. Workers united can never be defeated.” The post Living wage, 2027 elections: NLC rallies workers for tough battles ahead appeared first on Vanguard News .

Discours du Trône : le double message du Roi au secteur financier
items.description: En appelant le secteur financier à mieux accompagner les PME, l'innovation, l'industrialisation et les exportations, tout en mobilisant davantage l'épargne nationale, le Roi Mohammed VI fixe une feuille de route articulée autour de deux priorités complémentaires. Derrière ces orientations se dessine une stratégie destinée à financer une nouvelle phase de transformation économique reposant avant tout sur les ressources domestiques. Le passage consacré au secteur financier constitue l'un des axes majeurs du discours du Trône. Face à des besoins de financement qualifiés d'« envergure inédite », le Roi Mohammed VI appelle à une mobilisation accrue des ressources nationales et invite les acteurs financiers à accompagner plus efficacement l'investissement productif. Dans une analyse accordée à Hespress Fr, Azeddine Hannoun, professeur de droit public à la Faculté des sciences juridiques et politiques de l'Université Ibn Tofail, estime que ce passage « s'articule en réalité autour de deux demandes distinctes adressées au secteur financier, qu'il convient de bien distinguer » . Faciliter le financement des PME et de l'investissement productif La première demande royale porte sur « l'élargissement du financement bancaire et non bancaire aux PME, à l'innovation, à l'industrialisation et à l'exportation » , explique l'universitaire. Pour étayer cette lecture, il rappelle que les PME et TPE représentent entre 94 % et 95 % du tissu entrepreneurial marocain, soit près de 600.000 entreprises selon le Haut-Commissariat au Plan. Pourtant, elles ne captent qu'environ 30 % de l'encours total du crédit bancaire. Le professeur souligne également qu'une enquête menée en mai 2025 par la Banque européenne d'investissement et l'Union européenne montre que près de la moitié des PME marocaines restent en dehors du système bancaire formel. « Ce déséquilibre corrobore directement la thèse sur la domination persistante de l'investissement public » , observe-t-il, rappelant que le Pacte d'investissement 2022-2026 fixe pour objectif de porter la part de l'investissement privé aux deux tiers de l'investissement total d'ici à 2035, preuve que ce rééquilibrage reste encore à réaliser. Selon Azeddine Hannoun, le discours royal « prolonge et amplifie une dynamique déjà enclenchée plutôt qu'il n'ouvre un chantier entièrement nouveau » . L'universitaire cite notamment la Charte relative au financement des TPE signée en décembre 2025 à Rabat, le mécanisme de refinancement préférentiel instauré par Bank Al-Maghrib dès mars 2025 ainsi que le futur système national de scoring de crédit attendu courant 2026 pour réduire l'asymétrie d'information qui pénalise les petites entreprises dans l'accès au financement. M. Hannoun relève d'ailleurs que les derniers chiffres témoignent d'une accélération du crédit aux entreprises. Néanmoins, cette progression demeure, selon lui, « encore trop concentrée sur les grandes entreprises et le secteur public » , ce qui confirme la faible contribution du secteur privé à la croissance. Un appel à diversifier les sources de financement Le second volet du discours royal est, selon le professeur, d'une nature différente. Il concerne « la mobilisation de l'épargne institutionnelle et la redynamisation des marchés financiers » . Le Souverain vise ici moins le crédit bancaire traditionnel que la capacité des investisseurs institutionnels ( assurances, caisses de retraite et OPCVM ) à orienter une part plus importante de l'épargne nationale vers l'investissement productif et le marché boursier, plutôt que vers des placements jugés plus classiques, notamment la dette souveraine. Pour Azeddine Hannoun, il s'agit d'un appel à développer les mécanismes de financement non bancaire ou désintermédié, en renforçant le rôle du marché des capitaux, du capital-investissement et du financement obligataire des entreprises. L'universitaire replace enfin cette orientation dans le contexte économique décrit par le discours royal. En soulignant que « la dynamique de transformation économique et sociale exige la mobilisation de ressources financières d'une envergure inédite, dont l'essentiel doit provenir de financements domestiques » , le Souverain acte le fait que les ambitions du Royaume dépassent désormais les seules capacités budgétaires de l'État. Avec une croissance de 4,9 % en 2025, une industrialisation qui se poursuit et un secteur touristique ayant frôlé les 20 millions de visiteurs, le Maroc affiche des besoins de financement de plus en plus importants. « D'où la nécessité, assumée explicitement dans le discours, de faire porter davantage cet effort par l'épargne privée domestique plutôt que par la seule dépense publique ou l'endettement extérieur » , conclut le professeur. The post Discours du Trône : le double message du Roi au secteur financier appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Portrait – littérature : Pathé Dièye, écrire pour que les voix ne s’éteignent jamais
items.description: Ancien enfant de troupe du Prytanée militaire de Saint-Louis, passionné de lutte avant de devenir écrivain, Pathé Dièye construit une œuvre traversée par la mémoire, la quête de sens et l’attention portée aux choses simples. Entre roman, poésie et slam, il cherche moins à raconter le monde qu’à écouter les voix qui le composent. Pathé Dièye se présente comme un « sérieux collectionneur de rêves », un curieux qui cherche « le sacré dans les choses simples », une « trace d’éternité tentant de vivre à hauteur de sa lumière ». Derrière ces mots, il y a une manière d’habiter le monde. Celle typique d’un écrivain qui observe, questionne et transforme ses expériences en matière littéraire. Avant le monde des livres, Pathé a été un enfant des Parcelles Assainies. Dans cette banlieue dakaroise, il grandit entre deux univers. D’un côté, une famille attachée au savoir et à la discipline. De l’autre, une enfance de quartier rythmée par les jeux, les défis et les aventures quotidiennes. Il se souvient des billes, des « mbégués », des combats de lutte et des journées passées dehors avant de retrouver les cahiers. Il fallait apprendre à concilier ces deux mondes. Le jeune Pathé pouvait rentrer à la maison avec « une bouteille de billes, un ballon dégonflé », les pieds couverts de poussière après des heures de jeu, puis obtenir le lendemain les meilleures notes en classe. Cette enfance de liberté et d’exigence a façonné un caractère où la curiosité intellectuelle côtoie l’énergie du terrain. Mais il y avait aussi l’arène. Avant les livres, il y a eu la lutte, comme cet « Appel des arènes » qui, comme un tocsin, ne cessait de l’appeler. « Patherson » (son sobriquet) raconte avec amusement que son grand-père maternel l’appelait Tyson en raison de ses qualités de lutteur. « La force des bras et la technicité ont mué pour se faire encre et plume. Peut-être… », sourit-il. Une phrase qui résume une trajectoire d’un enfant qui a changé d’arène sans abandonner le goût du combat. Ce rapport aux mots commence très tôt. Son enfance est peuplée de « dictionnaires particuliers ». Son père, son frère aîné et un ami beaucoup plus âgé remplissaient ce rôle. Lorsqu’il rencontrait un mot inconnu, il allait chercher sa signification auprès d’eux avant de l’inscrire dans un carnet. Le savoir circulait aussi dans les conversations. Sa relation au livre est un héritage familial. Chez lui, l’ouvrage mérite respect et attention. Son père répétait une consigne simple : les livres ne se cornent pas, on n’écrit pas dessus. Cette éducation a construit une relation intime avec la lecture. Pathé garde encore l’image des livres anciens de son père, conservés avec soin malgré les années, avec leurs pages jaunies et leur odeur particulière. « J’ai commencé à lire comme on entre dans un lieu saint », explique-t-il. Lire constitue dès lors une rencontre avec soi-même, et une manière de trouver des outils pour comprendre et transformer le monde. L’écriture, elle, s’impose progressivement. Pathé ne se rappelle pas son premier texte. Il se rappelle plutôt les nombreux carnets remplis de ratures, de vers inachevés, de fragments et de rêves conservés. Écrire est devenu une manière d’enregistrer ce qui traverse son esprit et ce qui attire son regard. « L’acte d’écrire est depuis longtemps un appareil photo pour moi », dit-il. Les premières voix qui l’ont poussé vers l’écriture ne sont pas celles des grands auteurs, mais celles de son enfance. La voix de sa mère qui l’encourageait à lire. Celle de son frère aîné qui écrivait et déclamait des poèmes dans la maison. Celle de son père expliquant une règle de grammaire à partir d’un objet du quotidien ou d’une scène ordinaire. « J’ai écrit un roman, je ne sais pas de quoi ça parle » « J’ai eu envie d’écrire pour que ces voix, jamais, ne s’éteignent dans ma tête », confie-t-il. Cette phrase résume peut-être le moteur profond de son œuvre. Écrire, c’est conserver une mémoire, prolonger une transmission et donner une nouvelle existence à ceux qui ont contribué à construire son regard. Plus tard, des écrivains comme Yasmina Khadra, Driss Ksikes, Elif Shafak, Milan Kundera ou Frankétienne nourrissent son imaginaire. Mais Patherson refuse l’idée d’une vocation construite de manière linéaire. Le roman, dit-il, ne relève pas d’un choix calculé. « Il m’est tombé dessus », affirme-t-il. Son premier roman, « J’ai écrit un roman, je ne sais pas de quoi ça parle », porte déjà cette volonté de sortir des cadres habituels. Le titre lui-même traduit son rapport particulier à la création. Derrière cette apparente provocation se cache une réflexion sur les récits politiques, sur la manière dont les sociétés racontent leurs histoires et sur la complexité des vies humaines. Le livre est né d’un travail de réflexion sur les récits du politique. Pathé Dièye y interroge la tendance à réduire les réalités sociales à des chiffres alors que les existences humaines sont beaucoup plus complexes. Il observe aussi ces espaces sénégalais de rencontre que sont les « cars rapides », les carrefours, les lieux religieux et les territoires traversés par les confréries. Dans son écriture, les personnages ordinaires occupent une place centrale. « Ils font la vie. Enlevez-les, il ne reste plus rien », assure-t-il. Son regard se pose sur ceux qui composent la société dans sa diversité, ceux dont les histoires sont parfois peu visibles mais qui racontent une époque. Cette attention au quotidien traverse aussi sa poésie. Dans « L’irrésistible attrait de l’ordinaire », Pathé Diéye choisit de faire du simple une matière poétique. Pour lui, la poésie permet de dépasser l’idée de banalité et de regarder autrement ce qui semble insignifiant. Le recueil est aussi une forme de résistance. L’écrivain explique avoir voulu lutter contre « la dictature de l’ailleurs et du plus » comme promesse permanente d’un bonheur futur. Il célèbre au contraire l’ici et maintenant, l’ordinaire comme espace possible des rêves, des utopies et des transformations. Avec « Accoucher de soi », il poursuit cette exploration intérieure. Le titre traduit une naissance artistique et personnelle. Cet « accouchement » représente une rébellion face aux injonctions à être, une recherche de liberté et une affirmation progressive de sa voix. Le recueil marque pour lui une étape où il assume davantage son ton et sa posture d’auteur. La poésie et le slam occupent une place importante dans cette construction. Ils prolongent son rapport premier à la voix. Chez Patherson, les mots sont aussi faits pour être entendus, partagés et incarnés. Son style, il refuse de le considérer comme définitif. Il évolue avec lui. Aujourd’hui, il revendique la spontanéité et l’abandon. Il écrit partout : dans les cimetières, au sport, au milieu de la nuit, au marché, à l’église, à la mer. Mais derrière l’écrivain qui affirme sa voix demeure le doute. Un doute qu’il considère comme nécessaire. « Si la vocation est une partition musicale, le doute en est le refrain », explique-t-il. Cette interrogation permanente nourrit son exigence d’être fidèle à ce qui résonne en lui et de rester sincère dans son écriture. Pathé Dièye évolue ainsi entre plusieurs univers : chercheur, romancier, poète, slameur et observateur de la société. Son parcours raconte une transformation. L’enfant qui luttait dans les rues des Parcelles Assainies n’a pas abandonné le combat. Il l’a simplement déplacé. Désormais, son arène est celle des mots. Ses adversaires sont les questions, les idées reçues et les oublis. Ses armes sont l’encre, la poésie et les histoires qu’il porte. Écrire pour lui reste une manière de garder vivantes les voix qui l’ont construit. Par Amadou KÉBÉ

items.title: Troops foil kidnap attempts, rescue Zamfara polytechnic rector
items.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau Troops of Sector 2, Joint Task Force North West, Operation FANSAN YAMMA, have foiled multiple kidnap attempts and rescued the Rector of the Federal Polytechnic, Kaura Namoda, Zamfara State. The Media Information Officer of the Joint Task Force, Lt.-Col. Aliyu Danja, disclosed this in a statement, saying the operation followed a distress call in the early hours of Tuesday over terrorist activities around Tsohon-Tasha Street in Kaura Namoda Local Government Area. According to the statement, the attackers had invaded the residence of the rector, Dr. Aminu Yusuf, killing his private security guard and injuring another resident before attempting to abduct the rector and members of his family. Danja said troops responded swiftly and engaged the attackers with superior firepower, forcing them to flee and abandon their victims. “The rector and his family were rescued unharmed,” he said. In a separate operation on the same day, troops on night patrol responded to another distress call from Tungan Dorawa community in Barkeji Village over an attempted abduction by terrorists. Despite the difficult terrain, Danja said the troops pursued the fleeing suspects, engaged them, and foiled the kidnap attempt. He added that the troops simultaneously confronted another group of attackers in the same community who were attempting to abduct a prominent businessman, Alhaji Azaria. “The prompt intervention forced the terrorists to flee and abandon their mission. Alhaji Azaria, along with 21 other civilians abducted from neighbouring houses, were rescued,” the statement said. Meanwhile, troops also arrested a suspected terrorist informant, identified as 45-year-old Falalu Yusuf, who is believed to have collaborated with the attackers. The suspect has been handed over to the appropriate authorities for further investigation and necessary action. Operation FANSAN YAMMA commended the vigilance, courage and professionalism of the troops, reaffirming its commitment to restoring peace and security in Zamfara State and the wider North-West region. The post Troops foil kidnap attempts, rescue Zamfara polytechnic rector appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: FIFA proposal ‘an opportunity but not an obligation’ – Infantino
items.description: FIFA president Gianni Infantino said Wednesday that the proposed launch of a private subsidiary to exploit the commercial benefits of the World Cup was “an opportunity but not an obligation”. A proposal to sell stakes in FIFA’s major competitions sparked disbelief and outrage globally since it was revealed Tuesday, but Infantino defended the idea, saying too little of football’s commercial value reached the parts of the game that need it most. “FIFA Forward Enterprise, or FFE, is actually a proposal, an offer. It’s part of a democratic process – a consultation process – and, above all, it is an opportunity but not an obligation,” Infantino said in a video released Wednesday evening. “It is a golden opportunity to turbocharge the development of the game globally. But again, it is just an offer, not an obligation.” Infantino insisted the proposal was centred on unlocking “previously uncaptured commercial value” and was conditional on a democratic vote of FIFA’s 211 member associations and approval by the FIFA council. “Capturing that value requires additional expertise, additional insight, distinct from governing and developing the sport,” he said. “It would simply commercialise and organise all FIFA-owned competitions along with sponsorship, broadcast, licensing and new ventures for the benefit of FIFA’s 211 member associations.” Infantino said the game would not change and the fans would be happier. “Fans from everywhere in the world would gain immeasurably from this game-changing potential because it will transform football in their countries,” he said. AFP The post FIFA proposal ‘an opportunity but not an obligation’ – Infantino appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: FESTAC Power Outage: EKEDP blames cable vandalism, transmission upgrades
items.description: By Uzoma Marvellous The prolonged power outage affecting FESTAC Town, Amuwo Odofin and neighbouring communities is the result of ongoing transmission upgrades and persistent vandalism of underground electricity cables, Eko Electricity Distribution Plc (EKEDP) has said. In a statement yesterday, the General Manager, Corporate Communications, EKEDP, Abiola Aloba, said the supply disruption was caused mainly by improvement works at the national transmission level, with repeated cable vandalism worsening the situation. He said: “Recent supply challenges in FESTAC have been driven principally by upgrades and improvement activities at the national transmission level. These outages were, however, compounded by sustained vandalism of underground distribution cables.” According to Aloba, the FESTAC axis “regrettably records the highest incidence” of underground cable vandalism across the EKEDP network. He disclosed that the company had taken steps to improve electricity supply, including completing and commissioning the FESTAC 3 feeder, which will provide an alternative source of power from the Ojo Transmission Station. According to him, “The new FESTAC 3 feeder, radiating from Ojo Transmission Station to provide an alternative source of supply to FESTAC Town, has been completed and commissioned, with energisation awaiting final load-balancing arrangements and TCN approvals.” Aloba added that supply on the FESTAC 1 33kV feeder had been partially restored after engineers isolated a faulty underground cable, while fault location and restoration work continue daily. He said EKEDP had invested hundreds of millions of naira in the FESTAC network to improve electricity supply and strengthen infrastructure. On security, Aloba said the company had escalated the vandalism of its facilities to the Lagos State Police Command. He stated: “The Company has escalated the vandalism crisis to the highest levels of the Lagos State Police Command, with arrests already made and suspects in custody.” The development comes amid growing concerns among residents and businesses over the prolonged blackout in FESTAC, Amuwo Odofin and adjoining communities. Aloba said EKEDP had continued to engage residents, community leaders, the FESTAC District Business Manager, the traditional institution of Amuwo Odofin and the local government to address the situation. He noted that the company’s “door remains open to every resident and recognised community body through established channels.” While acknowledging the constitutional right of residents to peaceful protest, he appealed for calm and urged all parties to ensure that engagements remain lawful. “The Company appeals to all parties to keep every form of engagement lawful, respectful and safe for residents, staff and electricity infrastructure alike, so that the shared goal of stable power supply is not set back by avoidable disruption,” he said. EKEDP reaffirmed its commitment to restoring and sustaining improved electricity supply to FESTAC and neighbouring communities, assuring customers that it would continue to provide updates on restoration efforts. items.title: At least 11 killed, 6 injured as three-storey building collapses in Lahore's Harbanspura
items.description: LAHORE: At least 11 people of the same family were killed and six injured after a three-story building collapsed in Lahore’s Harbanspura late on Wednesday, according to authorities. Spokesperson for the Lahore deputy commissioner Harris Ali confirmed to Dawn that the death toll of the incident had risen to 11 after rescue workers pulled out the body of an elderly woman. Meanwhile, he said the operation at the site was still ongoing on Thursday afternoon as a minor girl was believed to be still under the rubble. The spokesperson said three brothers and their families were residing in the building, and they were joined by their sister and her children for a birthday celebration on Wednesday night, following which the structure collapsed. “The building collapsed floor by floor from the top down,” he said. The cause of the collapse is yet to be determined, for which Lahore DC retired Capt Muhammad Ali Ijaz has ordered an inquiry, a statement issued by his office said. The statement said he was supervising the rescue operation at the site of the incident, adding that Rescue 1122 teams, assisted by district administration officials, were clearing the debris. Heavy machinery had also been deployed to speed up the operation, it said. According to the statement, the DC directed the relevant officials at the site to ensure the safe recovery of all those trapped under the debris. The incident comes a month after a roof collapse at a tuition centre in Lahore’s Kahna area claimed the lives of 14 children. Police had registered a case against the tuition centre’s owners and the building’s contractor a day after the incident, with the first information report stating that the suspects were putting soil on the dilapidated building’s roof, which collapsed because of the extra load. In a similar incident in early May, four children were killed and 20 people injured after the roof of a classroom at a private school in Dera Ghazi Khan collapsed. A probe into the incident revealed that construction for an extension of the building was under way when the roof of the classroom collapsed. According to the district administration’s incident report, the roof was overloaded as sand and bricks were placed on it, and it could not bear the load and consequently collapsed.

items.title: Shell profits double as oil prices rise due to Iran war
items.description: Shell’s profits for the second quarter of the year have more than doubled after the Iran war pushed up oil prices. The oil giant’s profits for the April-to-June period reached $9.84bn (£7.37bn) – up from $4.26bn at the same point last year. The price of oil has soared since the outbreak of the US-Israel war with Iran due to major disruption to global supplies of oil and liquid natural gas (LNG) through the Strait of Hormuz. Shell chief executive Wael Sawan said the company’s “operational performance enabled very strong results during another quarter of severe disruption in global energy markets”. Together with its profits of $6.92bn for the first three months of the year it means Shell has seen a 70% surge in first-half earnings. Shell and other energy giants such as BP and Norway’s Equinor have seen bumper profits this year, partly down to trading on oil price swings. Before the conflict began, the price of Brent crude, the global benchmark for oil prices, was around $73 a barrel. Since then, it has peaked above $120 but also fallen back below $100 as speculation has swirled over when the Strait of Hormuz will reopen. These big movements in the oil price can widen the gap between buying and selling prices which typically enables traders to make bigger profits.

items.title: Ex-Kano LG chairman returns to tailoring after court ouster
items.description: Former Kumbotso Local Government Chairman in Kano State, Abdullahi Gali Shitu, popularly known as Comrade Abdullahi Gali Basaf, has returned to tailoring full-time after losing his office through a court ruling, saying the trade offers greater stability than politics. Basaf, who served as Kumbotso chairman until March 2026, told Daily Trust that his decision was intended to send a message that politicians should have a sustainable trade and see politics as an opportunity for service rather than a permanent source of livelihood. “Tailoring is not a small trade. It is a major one. It sustains livelihoods. Even in politics, my tailoring business helped me financially to support my campaigns and organisations,” he said. The former council chairman currently runs a tailoring shop in Sheka Ward that employs about 20 people. He said he plans to modernise the business, establish a garment company, and create jobs for more than 50 people. “My goal is to modernise tailoring, establish a garment company, and employ 50 or more people. I want to contribute to the economy,” he said. Basaf said he wants young people to see dignity in skilled trades and not despise vocational work. “Value your trade more than politics, because it sustains you and enables you to support your political activities,” he advised. A graduate with Bachelor’s and Master’s degrees in Political Science, Basaf said he chose tailoring out of passion despite having opportunities for white-collar jobs. Basaf’s political career was closely linked to the Kwankwasiyya movement. He founded Kwankwasiyya Reporters in 2015, served as chairman of the Alliance National Party in Kano, contested for the Senate in 2019, and later joined the NNPP, where he was appointed Senior Special Assistant on Information. He won the Kumbotso chairmanship election in 2024, but the Kano State High Court nullified his Certificate of Return in March 2026 and declared Ali Musa, known as Hardworker, the rightful winner. Reflecting on life after office, Basaf described tailoring as “a noble profession, even greater than holding political office.” “Politics can change overnight. You can be in the office today and out tomorrow. But tailoring remains. It feeds you, it supports your family, and it allows you to help others,” he said. Although he has returned fully to tailoring, Basaf said he is not abandoning politics entirely, insisting that public engagement remains part of his life. items.title: TETFund cracks down on abandoned projects
items.description: ….Bars defaulting institutions from 2027 funding By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Tertiary Education Trust Fund,TETFund, has wielded the big stick against beneficiary tertiary institutions that have failed to complete intervention projects. It also announced that institutions with lingering abandoned or delayed projects would be shut out of new project approvals under the 2027 intervention cycle. The tough stance was adopted by the Board of Trustees, BoT, of the Fund as part of sweeping measures aimed at ending years of project delays, cost overruns and poor implementation that have undermined the impact of TETFund interventions across Nigeria’s tertiary institutions. The Fund’s Director, Public Affairs, Abdulmumin Oniyangi, who disclosed this in a statement yesterday, quoted Chairman of the Board, Aminu Bello Masari, as saying “the era of allowing institutions to pile up fresh projects while existing ones remain uncompleted was over.” Masari, who noted that the Board would no longer tolerate what it described as avoidable delays, acknowledged that some of the stalled projects were initially affected by soaring prices of construction materials, including cement, reinforcement bars, sanitary and electrical fittings. He recalled that the Board had introduced a special intervention line in 2023 to address such projects. According to him, the initiative recorded significant success, with many previously abandoned projects completed after additional funding was provided. Despite that intervention, he lamented that delays had continued in several institutions, blaming the trend largely on lack of continuity by successive heads of institutions who abandoned inherited projects in favour of new ones, as well as bureaucratic bottlenecks that slow payments to contractors. He warned that internal politics and administrative red tape within beneficiary institutions would no longer be allowed to frustrate projects financed with public funds. To permanently address the challenge, the Board approved a raft of immediate measures. Under the new directives, every beneficiary institution must compile a comprehensive inventory of all projects that have remained uncompleted for more than six months beyond their scheduled completion dates, clearly stating the reasons for the delays and proposing practical solutions. The institutions are also required to rank the projects according to priority and relevance, while providing detailed cost estimates needed for their completion. In addition, each institution is to establish a robust project supervision mechanism involving its physical planning and maintenance departments to ensure projects are delivered on schedule, within approved costs and according to required quality standards. Most significantly, institutions with delayed projects will now be compelled to channel their annual, zonal and high impact intervention allocations towards completing those projects before seeking approval for any new ones. The Board declared that no fresh projects would be admitted for any institution identified as having outstanding delayed projects during the 2027 intervention cycle. To ensure compliance, TETFund disclosed that monitoring teams made up of Board members and the Fund’s technical officials would embark on nationwide inspections of affected projects between August and September 2026. The inspections, the Fund said, would assess the status of the projects and evaluate completion plans submitted by beneficiary institutions ahead of the Board’s statutory meeting in October 2026, where projects to be included in the 2027 disbursement guidelines would be considered.
